text:
# SEO / AEO 实操蓝图：站外链接与 AI 提及

- 作者：Sebastien（@sebastien_t_）
- 发布时间：2026-10-11 16:34（北京时间）
- 原帖：https://x.com/sebastien_t_/status/2109200884894699746
- 原文标题（网页显示）：7 years of SEO/AEO, one blueprint: earn links and AI mentions without wasting a week (Part 2, off-si
- 说明：中文全文翻译，后附英文原文。文中数据、观点及推广内容均为作者表述，未经独立验证。

---

![原文配图](../../90_附件/GEO国外近期实操_20261028第三批_配图/2109200884894699746-封面.jpg)

## 中文全文

第一部分讲了你自己网站上的所有工作。第二部分讲网站之外的一切：链接、提及，以及 AI 助手引用的页面。下面是我们的智能体现在遵循的方法，以及它本周在我们的博客分析中发现的情况。

如果你错过了第一部分，先简单介绍一下背景。做 IZeat 之前，我在自己搭建的网站上做了约 7 年的 SEO 和 AEO：3 个垂直电商网站、1 个 SaaS 和 1 个博客。现在，Laetitia 和我一起开发 IZeat，这是一款五星级厨师热量追踪工具：它会根据你当天剩余的热量额度，推荐让人有饱腹感的餐食；你还可以在 ChatGPT、Claude 或其他助手中，用一句话记录自己吃了什么。我们的智能体 Claude Code 和 Codex 撰写了大部分公开页面，其中包括一个有 66 篇文章的博客。

谈到站外工作，大多数建议最后都会变成“建设反向链接”。这并不是一种方法，也是智能体最容易浪费时间的地方：它们可能兴致勃勃地列出 200 个永远不会回复的网站。所以，我们先把方法写下来，于 10 月 5 日和 6 日在自己的博客上手动执行，只留下真正能推进工作的做法。

# 不知道从哪里开始？先看搜索结果，再为每一条结果确定一个动作

## 从每个页面的目标关键词出发，查看它的 Google 搜索结果页

并非每个页面都需要站外工作。拿出某个页面的目标关键词，在 Google 中搜索，查看搜索引擎结果页（SERP）。排在上面的内容，会告诉你这个页面需要什么：

| 该关键词的 Google 搜索结果中排着什么 | 页面需要什么 | 站外工作 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 榜单、评测、对比文章、论坛讨论串（“最佳 X”“X 的替代方案”“X 与 Y 对比”） | 被加入这些页面 | 联系作者，在讨论串中回答 |
| 比你的页面强得多的页面，而且没有可以加入的榜单 | 来自其他网站的链接 | 客座文章、资源页面、你自己的数据，或者获取指向支柱页面并能向下传递到该页面的链接 |
| 质量较弱的页面，竞争难度低 | 不需要站外工作 | 在追踪显示页面遇到瓶颈之前，不做站外工作 |

然后，从价值最高的关键词开始：用月搜索量乘以每次点击费用，也就是广告主已经愿意为这类搜索支付的费用。面临最激烈竞争的关键词留到第二轮。

我们的博客里，66 篇文章分别针对 66 个关键词。其中 40 个关键词的搜索结果显示不需要站外工作；另外 26 个需要。我们处理了其中 21 个，竞争最激烈的 5 个暂时留待后续。

## 查看两类信息：Google 搜索结果和 AI 助手的来源

1. **当天实时的 Google 搜索结果。**关键词工具导出的结果只是起点，不是真相：两天之间，我们的一个搜索结果页就失去了 AI Overview，前 10 名也发生了变化。
2. **AI 助手针对同一关键词所引用的来源。**我们使用 Google AI Overview、未登录状态的 ChatGPT 和 Claude。我们不再使用 Perplexity，因为我们的客户使用的是 ChatGPT 和 Claude。

## 每条结果都对应一个动作；否则就记录原因并放弃

| 在搜索结果页或 AI 来源中发现了什么 | 怎么做 | 在哪里做 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 中立网站上的榜单或对比文章 | 给作者发邮件，请求加入，并给出他们会在意的理由 | 对方网站 |
| 中立文章，但不是榜单 | 提供一个可加入的章节、一段引述或你的数据 | 对方网站 |
| 一条开放且近期的论坛讨论 | 如果论坛规则允许，以创始人身份回答 | 论坛 |
| 竞争对手在自己博客上发布的榜单 | 不要联系他们。把自己的页面做成搜索结果中最好的榜单，再查看哪些页面链接到他们的榜单，并用这张表逐一处理这些页面 | 先在你的网站，再在对方网站 |
| 某个平台上有人凭自己的帖子获得排名 | 在该平台发布你自己的版本 | 该平台 |
| 没有可执行的动作 | 放弃，并记录原因 | 追踪表 |

最后一行的重要性比看上去更大。我们会把每一个动作以及每一条被放弃的结果和放弃原因，记录在关键词表中对应页面的那一行里，这样下个月就不会有人再次检查它。

# 榜单都由竞争对手掌握？真正的目标是中立榜单

对于“X 的替代方案”和“最佳 X 应用”这类关键词，搜索结果中的大多数榜单都由竞争对手写在自己的博客上。在“myfitnesspal alternative”（MyFitnessPal 替代方案）的 Google 前 10 名中，每一篇榜单都来自某个应用或近似的竞争对手，并把自己排在榜单里。他们绝不会把你加进去，因此给他们发邮件只会浪费一周。这里的工作要放在你自己的网站上：你的页面必须胜过他们的榜单。

在你的网站之外，剩下的目标是中立来源：

- **亲自测试应用的独立评测者和教练。**一位营养师的对比文章为列出的每个应用都提供了可传递权重的链接：如果她把你加进去，你就能获得一条真正的反向链接。
- **会测试应用的媒体榜单。**有些媒体确实会测试；先阅读它们的测试方法部分。Forbes Health 的热量计算应用榜单只收录 App Store 和 Google Play 上的应用。一个运行在 ChatGPT 或 Claude 内的产品，邮件还没被读到就已经不符合条件。
- **已经评测你所在品类的创作者，包括视频创作者。**一位营养师在 YouTube 上为 6 款营养应用做的排名，成为了 Google AI Overview 的一个来源。

在 AI 助手引用的来源中，有两种情况让我感到意外：

- Claude 凭记忆回答“myfitnesspal alternative”，完全没有给出来源。因此没有任何对象可以联系。对于 Claude，能否被提及取决于它学习过的页面，这是一场长期工作。
- ChatGPT 有好几次引用了“独立评测团队”的内容，但这些来源没有联系页面、没有导出链接，也没有署名作者。我们没有联系它们，也不会自己做一个这样的站。我们选择在自己的网站上制作对比页面，并进行真实测试。

我们保留下来的规则是：给任何人发邮件之前，先打开对方的页面，找到作者，检查日期，看看它是否链接到榜单中的应用，并找到真实的联系方式。如果其中某一项缺失，通常就放弃。

# Reddit、Medium、LinkedIn：哪里可以发帖，哪里会被封禁

论坛讨论串会出现在搜索结果中，AI 助手也会阅读它们。因此，在写任何一条评论之前，我们都会先阅读各论坛的规则。

| 平台或社区 | 我们的发现（2026 年 10 月） |
| --- | --- |
| 饮食和健身类 subreddit | 我们打开的 4 个社区全部禁止推广应用；其中一个警告会永久封禁且不接受申诉。现在我们遇到这些社区会直接跳过，连讨论串都不打开 |
| 品牌 subreddit | 不容忍推广其他应用 |
| 某个应用的 subreddit | 创始人明确披露自身身份后，其评论获得了允许 |
| 投稿型网站 | 有一个网站接受免费投稿，但只有赞助文章才保证提供链接，价格从 130 美元起 |

由此得出了三条规则：

- **每次都说明你是谁。**冒充客户或使用第二个账号不属于灰色地带。在欧盟，经营者把自己伪装成消费者属于不公平行为，虚假评价也是如此。
- **论坛规则优先。**如果禁止链接或推广，就提供不带链接的建议，或者不参与。
- Reddit 或 LinkedIn 的链接通常是 nofollow，直接传递的权重很少。它们能带来的是访问、更快地被发现、AI 助手会读取的提及，以及读者之后引用你的页面时获得的链接。

在别人的平台上发布你自己的内容也算。我们向一个投稿型网站提交了一篇署名文章，因为同一网站上一篇投稿文章，正是 ChatGPT 针对我们某个关键词所引用的来源之一。

# 付出了努力却没有收获？有些关键词无法通过站外工作取胜

这一部分帮我们节省了最多时间。在处理过的 21 个关键词中，有 13 个在网站外没有新的联系对象。除了竞争对手掌握的榜单之外，它们可以分为四类：

1. **健康问题。**“how many calories should I eat a day”（我每天应该摄入多少卡路里）的搜索结果被卫生机构和医院占据，ChatGPT 引用的是美国膳食指南。无论邮件写什么，这些机构都不会链接到一个应用的博客。
2. **工具类关键词。**对于“nutrition calculator”（营养计算器），链接指向的是能搜索食物数据库的计算器。我们在 Ahrefs 中查看了其中被链接最多的工具的反向链接：共有 95 组链接，大多数来自把它当作营养成分数据来源的食谱博主。我们的计算器则是按比例换算用户从标签上输入的数值。两者是不同的服务，因此没有人会把自己的链接换成指向我们的网站。解决办法在于我们网站上的产品，而不是对外联系。
3. **你不符合条件的榜单。**生酮应用榜单以净碳水追踪能力为筛选条件；IZeat 记录热量和三大营养素，但不记录净碳水。“最佳免费”榜单要求有免费方案；IZeat 提供试用，之后需要付费。请求加入这样的榜单，第一关就会失败。
4. **只围绕单一品牌的关键词。**“is MyFitnessPal free”（MyFitnessPal 免费吗）的搜索结果是 MyFitnessPal 自己的帮助页面。没有第三方有理由提及你。

对于这 13 个关键词，工作回到了我们自己的网站上。针对每个页面，我们都记录搜索结果偏好什么、页面还缺什么，然后交给负责撰写博客的智能体。

# 两天工作取得了什么结果

10 月 5 日和 6 日，我们只使用免费工具，由智能体操作浏览器，得到了以下结果：

| 步骤 | 数量 |
| --- | ---: |
| 已整理的博客文章及其目标关键词 | 66 |
| 需要站外工作的关键词 | 26 |
| 已处理的关键词（竞争最激烈的 5 个留待后续） | 21 |
| 有中立网站或论坛可以联系的关键词 | 8 |
| 发给作者和编辑的消息 | 9 |
| 向投稿型网站提交的署名文章 | 1 |
| 在 Reddit 发布的创始人评论 | 1 |

每条消息都从同一段产品介绍出发，也就是我们在所有地方使用的那段介绍。只有第一条例外：智能体使用了一个较旧的产品定位来撰写。从那以后，它在每次起草之前都会重新阅读我们的营销参考资料。

目前还没有收到回复：预计一周后才会有回复。我会分享收到的结果，包括哪些方法没有奏效。

如果你曾为不在应用商店上架的产品做过对外联系：哪些榜单真正收录了你？

## 英文原文

Part 1 covered everything on your own site. Part 2 is everything outside it: links, mentions, and the pages AI assistants quote. Here's the method our agents now follow, and what it found on our blog this week.

Quick context if you missed Part 1. Before IZeat, I did SEO and AEO for about 7 years on sites I built myself: 3 niche e-commerce sites, 1 SaaS and 1 blog. Today Laetitia and I build IZeat, the five-star chef calorie tracker: it suggests satisfying meals that fit what you have left today, and you log what you ate in one sentence, from ChatGPT, Claude or any other assistant. Our agents, Claude Code and Codex, write most of our public pages, including a blog of 66 articles.

Off-site is where most advice turns into "build backlinks". That's not a method, and it's where agents waste the most time: they'll happily list 200 sites that will never answer. So we wrote the method first, ran it by hand on our blog on 5 and 6 October, and kept only what led somewhere.

# Don't know where to start? Read the SERP, then give every result one action

## Start from the keyword each page targets, and read its Google SERP

Not every page needs off-site work. Take the keyword a page targets, search it on Google, and read the SERP. What ranks there tells you what the page needs:

| What ranks in the Google SERP for that keyword | What the page needs | Off-site work |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lists, reviews, comparisons, forum threads ("best X", "X alternatives", "X vs Y") | To be added to those pages | Contact the authors, answer the threads |
| Pages much stronger than yours, and no list to join | Links from other sites | Guest articles, resource pages, your own data, or links to a pillar that pass down to the page |
| Weak pages, low difficulty | Nothing outside | None until tracking shows the page stuck |

Then start with the keywords worth the most: monthly volume × cost per click, what advertisers already pay for that search. Keywords facing the strongest competition wait for a second wave.

On our blog, 66 articles target 66 keywords. For 40, the SERP called for no off-site work. For 26, it did. We worked through 21 of them; the 5 facing the strongest competition wait.

## Read two things: the Google SERP and the AI assistants' sources

1. The Google SERP, live, the day you work. A keyword-tool export is a starting point, not the truth: between two days, one of our SERPs lost its AI Overview and its top 10 changed.
2. The sources AI assistants cite for the same keyword. We use Google AI Overview, ChatGPT logged out and Claude. Perplexity went out: our customers use ChatGPT and Claude.

## Every result triggers one action, or it's dropped with a reason

| What you find in the SERP or the AI sources | What to do | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A neutral site with a list or comparison | Email the author to be added, with a reason they care about | On their site |
| A neutral article that isn't a list | Offer a section, a quote or your data | On their site |
| An open, recent forum thread | Answer as the founder, if the forum's rules allow it | On the forum |
| A competitor's list on its own blog | Don't contact them. Make your own page the best list in the SERP, then look at who links to theirs and run each of those pages through this table | On your site, then on theirs |
| A platform where someone ranks with their own post | Publish your own version there | On that platform |
| Nothing to act on | Drop it and write down why | In your tracking sheet |

The last row matters more than it looks. We record every action and every dropped result, with its reason, in the row of the page in our keyword sheet, so nobody checks it again next month.

# Competitors own the lists? The real targets are the neutral ones

For "X alternatives" and "best X app" keywords, most of the lists in the SERP are written by competitors, on their own blogs. On "myfitnesspal alternative", every list in Google's top 10 came from an app, or a near-competitor, ranking itself. They will never add you, so emailing them is a week lost. The work there happens on your own site: your page has to beat their lists.

Outside your site, the targets that remain are the neutral ones:

- Independent reviewers and coaches who test apps themselves. One dietitian's comparison linked to every app it listed with followed links: a real backlink if she adds you.
- Media lists that test apps. Some do; read their method section first. Forbes Health's calorie-counter list only covers apps from the App Store and Google Play. A product that lives inside ChatGPT or Claude is out before anyone reads the email.
- Creators who already review your category, video included. A dietitian's YouTube ranking of six nutrition apps was a source of Google's AI Overview.

Two patterns surprised me in the AI assistants' sources:

- Claude answered "myfitnesspal alternative" from memory, with no source at all. There was nothing to contact. For Claude, being mentioned depends on the pages it learned from, which is a long game.
- ChatGPT several times cited "independent review desks" with no contact page, no outbound link and no named author. We didn't contact them, and we won't build one. What we build instead is our own comparison page, on our site, with a real test.

The rule we kept: before emailing anyone, open their page, find the author, check the date, check whether it links to the apps it lists, and find a real contact. If one of those is missing, it's usually a drop.

# Reddit, Medium, LinkedIn: where you can post, and where you'll get banned

Forum threads rank in the SERP, and AI assistants read them. So before writing a single comment, we read each forum's rules.

| Where | What we found (October 2026) |
| --- | --- |
| Diet and fitness subreddits | All four we opened ban promoting an app; one threatens a permanent ban with no appeal. We now skip them without opening the thread |
| Brand subreddits | Promoting another app isn't tolerated |
| An app subreddit | A comment from the founder, disclosed as such, was allowed |
| Contributor sites | One accepts free submissions, but only guarantees a link in a sponsored post, from $130 |

Three rules came out of it:

- Say who you are, every time. A fake customer or a second account isn't a grey zone. In the EU, presenting yourself as a consumer when you're the trader is an unfair practice, and so are false reviews.
- The forum's rules come first. If links or promotion are banned, give the advice without a link, or stay out.
- Links from Reddit or LinkedIn are usually nofollow. They pass little authority directly. What they bring is visits, faster discovery, mentions the assistants read, and links earned later when a reader cites your page.

Publishing your own content on someone else's platform counts too. We submitted a signed article to a contributor site, because a contributor post on that same site was among the sources ChatGPT cited for one of our keywords.

# Putting in the effort and nothing comes back? Some keywords can't be won off-site

This part saved us the most time. Out of the 21 keywords we worked, 13 had nobody new to contact outside our site. Apart from lists owned by competitors, they fall into four groups:

1. Health questions. The SERP for "how many calories should I eat a day" is held by health authorities and hospitals, and ChatGPT cites the US Dietary Guidelines. None of them will link to an app's blog, whatever the email says.
2. Tool keywords. For "nutrition calculator", the links go to calculators that search a food database. We read the backlinks of the most-linked one in Ahrefs: 95 groups of links, mostly recipe bloggers citing it as the source of their nutrition facts. Our calculator scales values you type in from a label. That's a different service, so nobody would swap their link for ours. The fix is in the product, on our site, not in outreach.
3. Lists with criteria you don't meet. Keto app lists choose on net-carb tracking; IZeat records calories and the three macros, without net carbs. "Best free" lists want a free plan; IZeat has a trial, then it's paid. Asking to be added would fail on the first line.
4. Keywords about one brand. The SERP for "is MyFitnessPal free" is MyFitnessPal's own help pages. No third party has a reason to mention you.

For those 13 keywords, the work moves back to our own site. For each page, we wrote a note on what its SERP rewards and what the page is missing, and handed it to the agent that writes the blog.

# What came out of two days

On 5 and 6 October, with free tools only and our agents driving the browser:

| Step | Count |
| --- | --- |
| Blog articles (and their target keywords) sorted | 66 |
| Keywords needing off-site work | 26 |
| Keywords worked (the 5 facing the strongest competition wait) | 21 |
| Keywords with a neutral site or forum to contact | 8 |
| Messages sent to authors and editors | 9 |
| Signed article submitted to a contributor site | 1 |
| Founder comment posted on Reddit | 1 |

Every message started from the same paragraph about the product, the one we use everywhere. Except the first: the agent wrote it from an older positioning. Since then, it rereads our marketing reference before every draft.

No replies yet: they're due after a week. I'll share what came back, including what didn't work.

If you've done outreach for a product that doesn't live in an app store: which lists actually took you?
